cols.title: The pipeline
cols.caption: Generation is this loop run once per token. Everything the model "knows" is inside the N blocks.

cols.title: What is a transformer?
items: A neural network that reads a **whole sequence of tokens at once** and learns which tokens matter to which.
The architecture behind GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama. ==Decoder-only== models predict the **next token**, again and again.
One block, repeated: **attention** (tokens talk to each other) + **MLP** (each token thinks on its own).

cols.title: Real-life analogy: a library search
text: **Query** = what this token is looking for.
**Key** = the label on every other token.
Best-matching labels pour in the most content.

cols.text: Attention is a **learned, soft lookup** that every token performs over the whole context. Nothing is fetched exactly; everything is mixed by weight.

cols.title: Attention, step by step
items: Each token vector `x` makes three new vectors: **Q** = x·W_Q, **K** = x·W_K, **V** = x·W_V (the W matrices are learned).
Score every pair: `score[i][j] = Q_i · K_j` → how much token i wants token j.
Scale by ==√d_k== (stops scores exploding), then **softmax** each row → weights that sum to 1.
Output for token i = the **weighted sum of all V_j**. High-weight tokens pour in more of their content.
Add it back onto `x` (the **residual**). The token now carries context.

cols.title: Formula box
cols.text:
Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax( Q·Kᵀ / √d_k ) · V

Shapes for T tokens, dim d: Q, K, V are (T × d); Q·Kᵀ is (T × T); the output is (T × d) again.

cols.title: Why an AI engineer cares
text: Cost is **O(T²)** in tokens → long prompts are expensive; that is why ==context engineering== exists.
K and V of the prompt are reused while generating (the **KV cache**) → that is what **prompt caching** sells you.
Context window = the largest T the model was trained to handle well.

left.title: It is NOT
items: A database lookup with exact keys
Reading left to right one word at a time (that is an RNN)
Aware of word order by itself
"Understanding" in the human sense

right.title: It IS
items: Soft matching: every token gets some weight
All tokens processed in parallel in each layer
Order added explicitly through positions
Next-token statistics learned from enormous text

pages.subtitle: Heads, blocks, code and interview prep

cols.title: Heads, masks, positions
items: **Multi-head**: several attention lookups run in parallel, each with its own W_Q/W_K/W_V (one head may track syntax, another coreference). Concatenate, project back.
**Causal mask**: in GPT a token may only look **left**. Future positions get −∞ before softmax → weight 0.
**Position**: attention is order-blind, so position is injected explicitly (learned positional embeddings in GPT-2, ==RoPE== in Llama and Qwen).

cols.title: One transformer block
cols.label: repeat N times (GPT-2 small: N = 12, 12 heads, d = 768)

layers.label: LayerNorm → MLP (expand 4×, GELU, project back) → + x

cols.caption: The "+ x" residual paths are why deep stacks train at all.

cols.title: Causal attention in 10 lines
cols.code:
import torch, math
T, d = 5, 16                 # tokens, dim
x = torch.randn(T, d)        # token vectors
Wq, Wk, Wv = [torch.randn(d, d) for _ in "qkv"]
Q, K, V = x @ Wq, x @ Wk, x @ Wv
s = Q @ K.T / math.sqrt(d)   # (T, T) scores
mask = torch.tril(torch.ones(T, T)).bool()
s = s.masked_fill(~mask, float("-inf"))
w = torch.softmax(s, dim=-1) # rows sum to 1
out = w @ V                  # mix of values
cols.caption: This is the whole idea. Everything else is stacking, normalising and scaling it up.

cols.title: Memory trick
cols.text:
**Q asks, K labels, V carries.**
Softmax shares out 100% of attention; the mask hides the future; positions tell the order.

cols.title: Quick revision points (last-minute)
groups: Tokens → vectors → N blocks → next-token probabilities.
Attention = softmax(QKᵀ/√d)·V, per token, over the whole context.
Q asks, K labels, V carries content.
Multi-head = parallel lookups; causal mask = look left only.
Order comes from positional info, not from attention.
Cost grows with T²; the KV cache makes generation cheap.
